title: Add post-install validation command for Private observability pack (metrics endpoints, Grafana API, rule loading)
author: Bruno Silva
description:
Context: As part of the “Private observability minimum pack” workstream, Solutions/SRE need a reliable post-install check that (a) the core /metrics endpoints are reachable, (b) Grafana is actually up and accepting API requests, and (c) PrometheusRule groups are being loaded (we’ve had multiple cases where rules exist in-cluster but never get picked up due to Operator/RBAC/config issues).

This PR adds a new installer CLI command: `redwood-private validate observability`.

What it validates (best-effort; works in air-gapped environments): 1) Metrics endpoints reachability: Checks service DNS + HTTP reachability for the expected component metrics endpoints (gateway, runtime, control plane, installer-health). For each endpoint we record status code, scrape duration, and whether the payload contains Prometheus exposition format headers. 2) Required signals presence: Runs a small set of “must-have” series checks by parsing a scrape sample (e.g., presence of `redwood_gateway_requests_total`, `redwood_runtime_decode_tokens_total`, `redwood_controlplane_reconcile_errors_total`, `redwood_installer_health_info`). This avoids needing a Prometheus query API in customer-managed setups. 3) Grafana API reachability: Validates that `/api/health` returns ok and that the configured auth works by calling `/api/org` (does not print token; token is read from env/flag or Kubernetes Secret). 4) Rule loading status: If the environment uses Prometheus Operator (detected via CRDs), we check that PrometheusRule objects exist for the pack and that they have been selected by a Prometheus instance (heuristics: label selectors + namespace + “rule evaluation” status where available). If a Prometheus URL is provided (`--prometheus-url`), we additionally query `/api/v1/rules` and verify the expected rule groups are present.

Output: Human-readable table by default + optional JSON report (`--output json`) suitable for attaching to support tickets / go-live checklists.

Security notes: - No secrets are logged; Grafana token is redacted in debug output and never emitted in JSON. - Kubernetes Secret reads are limited to the specific key configured via `--grafana-token-secret` (default: `grafana-admin` / `admin-password` is NOT assumed). - The validator is read-only: it does not mutate cluster state.

Flags: - `--namespace` (default: `redwood-private`) - `--grafana-url` and `--grafana-token` OR `--grafana-token-secret` - `--prometheus-url` (optional, for rule API checks) - `--timeout` / `--retries` - `--strict` (non-zero exit if any required check fails) - `--output table|json` and `--output-file`

Why now: This unblocks ENG-2852 (“supported signals checklist output in installer”) and addresses recurring upgrade issues (SUP-2431) where rule parsing/loading failures were discovered only after an incident drill.

Testing: - Unit tests for endpoint validation, secret redaction, and output formatting. - Kind-based CI smoke test: deploys minimal components + fake Grafana endpoint, runs validator in strict mode, asserts JSON schema and exit codes.

Follow-ups: - Wire this command into the installer post-install summary (ENG-2852). - Expand rule checks once the pack’s rule group naming is finalized in observability-pack (pending PR-322/323).
commits: installer/cli: add `validate observability` command scaffold + flag plumbing
validate: implement metrics endpoint probe + required-series checks
validate: add Grafana API health/auth checks with secret/token handling
validate: add PrometheusRule discovery + optional Prometheus /api/v1/rules verification
output: table + JSON renderer, exit codes, strict mode
ci: add kind-based smoke test job for validator
conversation:
Allison Grant (SRE): Can we make sure this fails hard only for the “must-have” checks? We don’t want customer-managed Prometheus setups to get a red build because /api/v1/rules isn’t available. Also please add explicit messaging when we fall back to scrape-based series detection.

Bruno Silva (author): Yep—made Prometheus API checks strictly optional behind `--prometheus-url`. Default path is scrape-based. Also added a “Mode” line in the report: `rules_check=crd_only` vs `rules_check=prom_api`.

Marcus Lin (Security): Please confirm we aren’t printing the Grafana token in debug logs. Also avoid defaulting to any “admin/admin” assumptions; the token/secret path should be explicit.

Bruno Silva (author): Confirmed. Token is never printed; redaction applied in debug dump. Removed old internal fallback that assumed admin creds. Users must provide `--grafana-token` or `--grafana-token-secret`.

Markus Klein (Solutions): Output is good, but can you include a short “next action” per failure? e.g., if metrics endpoint 403, suggest checking ServiceAccount/RBAC; if DNS fails, suggest checking NetworkPolicy.

Bruno Silva (author): Added per-check hints in table output and included `hint` field in JSON. Kept them generic so we don’t over-prescribe.

Sahana Iyer (CI): The kind test was flaky due to Grafana startup timing. Please add retries/backoff around the health endpoint.

Bruno Silva (author): Added `--retries` default (6) with exponential backoff for Grafana health and service endpoint probes. Kind test now waits on readiness before running strict mode.

Sergio Costa (Dashboards): Rule group name matching—please don’t hardcode exact names yet; the pack is still iterating.

Bruno Silva (author): Updated to match on label set (`redwood.io/observability-pack=true`) + namespace + group prefix `private-min-pack` (configurable). Left exact group list behind `--expected-rule-groups` for advanced use.

Final review: Allison approved after verifying strict-mode semantics and report output. Marcus approved after token handling changes. Merged via squash.
release_notes: Private installer: new `redwood-private validate observability` command to verify metrics reachability, Grafana API health/auth, and Prometheus rule loading (best-effort; supports air-gapped environments). Produces table or JSON report; supports strict mode for go-live validation.
